Panopticlick: Is your browser safe against tracking?

It's amazing the amount of difference noscript makes for that test. If I were really paranoid, I'd find out what the most generic user agent string is and adopt that too, but I've got a pretty non-unique fingerprint already.

Once you allow javascript pretty much any unique setting you have on your browser that can be detected by the server will make your browser unique or almost unique. Best to run a stock browser with a popular ad blocker if you want to avoid your browser being unique or almost unique. It's not an easy situation, because most people like to modify their browser. Running NoScript is great but since not many people in the world run it, it narrows the fingerprint down, then you couple that with what set of scripts each user allows narrows it down more.

There's no easy solutions. Javascript is horrible for privacy/anonymity.
